verses.text: Jehoshaphat had great wealth and honor. He made an alliance with Ahab by marriage.
Some years later, he went down to visit Ahab in Samaria. Ahab killed many sheep and cattle for him and the people with him, and he talked him into going with him to attack Ramoth Gilead.

Ahab king of Israel asked Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to attack Ramoth Gilead?" Jehoshaphat answered, "I am with you, and my people are like your people. We will join you in the war."
Then Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "But first, please ask what the LORD says."

So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and asked them, "Should we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or should I hold back?" They said, "Go, because God will hand it over to the king."
But Jehoshaphat asked, "Isn't there another prophet of the LORD here we can ask?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man we can ask the LORD through, but I hate him, because he never says anything good about me, only bad things. He is Micaiah son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say that."
So the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Quickly, bring Micaiah son of Imla."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting on their thrones, dressed in their royal robes. They were sitting in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying in front of them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made some iron horns and said, "The LORD says, 'With these you will push back the Syrians until they are destroyed.'"
All the prophets were saying the same thing: "Attack Ramoth Gilead and win, because the LORD will hand it over to the king."
The messenger who went to get Micaiah said to him, "Look, all the prophets are saying good things to the king with one voice. Please let your message agree with theirs, and say something good."
But Micaiah said, "As surely as the LORD lives, I will say what my God tells me."
When he came to the king, the king asked him, "Micaiah, should we go to war against Ramoth Gilead, or should I hold back?" He answered, "Go and win. They will be handed over to you."
The king said to him, "How many times must I make you promise to tell me nothing but the truth in the LORD's name?"
Then Micaiah said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These people have no master. Let each of them go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you he never says anything good about me, only bad?"
Micaiah said, "So listen to the LORD's message. I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, with all the armies of heaven standing on his right and on his left.
The LORD said, 'Who will trick Ahab king of Israel into attacking Ramoth Gilead so he will die there?' One said one thing, and another said something else.
Then a spirit came forward, stood in front of the LORD, and said, 'I will trick him.' The LORD asked him, 'How?'
He said, 'I will go and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.' The LORD said, 'You will trick him and succeed. Go and do it.'
So now, look, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of these prophets of yours. The LORD has decided that disaster will come to you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and slapped Micaiah on the face. He said, "Which way did the LORD's Spirit go when he left me to speak to you?"
Micaiah answered, "You will find out on the day you run into an inner room to hide."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and send him back to Amon, the governor of the city, and to Joash, the king's son.
Tell them, 'The king says: Put this man in prison. Give him nothing but a little bread and water until I come back safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you ever come back safely, then the LORD has not spoken through me." Then he added, "Remember this, all you people!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went to attack Ramoth Gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will go into battle in disguise, but you wear your royal robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.
The king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders, "Do not fight anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel."
When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That is the king of Israel!" So they turned to attack him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him.
When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they stopped chasing him.

But a soldier shot an arrow without aiming, and it hit the king of Israel between the pieces of his armor. The king told his chariot driver, "Turn around and get me out of the battle, because I am badly wounded."
The battle grew fierce all that day. The king of Israel held himself up in his chariot facing the Syrians until evening. At sunset he died.
